checks.note: createPaidStripeSubscription passes "sub-create-" + UUID.randomUUID() per call, and on a lost-response retry assertCanSubscribe/isOtherLiveSubscription only check the local row, which the orphaned first subscription never reached — so a second subscription is created and charged. Per the caveat: the reconciler itself isn't shown, but cancelStripeSubscriptionQuietly's comment calls it an "orphan alert," indicating alert-only, and the duplicate charge occurs regardless.

After a SCOUT downgrade, persistCoachCancellation voids all pending change rows, so changeCoachTier's newRank==currentRank branch (gated on pendingDowngrade) is a total no-op with no Stripe call, and persistCoachTierUpgrade never clears cancelAtPeriodEnd locally or at Stripe. No call in this file sends cancel_at_period_end=false; the one path that clears it (persistCoachSubscription) is blocked by assertCanSubscribe throwing alreadyActive while the row is still ACTIVE. Only caveat: an upgrade could incidentally clear the flag if StripeClient.updateSubscriptionTier (not shown) did so, but the re-select path is broken regardless.

The adapter's isPaidTierEntitled (lines 19–23) does map any existing row through SubscriptionEntitlement.isEntitled and defaults to true only when no row exists, consistent with the finding's premise — but the required verification (default status persisted by findOrCreateCoachSubscription, whether admin-provisioned coaches get payment rows, and reconcileMarketplaceTiers' findAll/SCOUT overwrite) depends on SubscriptionService, SubscriptionEntitlement, and repository code not shown.

applyCoachChange has no free-tier branch (unlike changeCoachTier, which maps a SCOUT target to cancelCoachSubscription): syncStripePriceForChange returns true when plan.priceId() is null, so phase 2 applies the SCOUT tier locally while the Stripe subscription is never updated or cancelled. The verification caveat (DB query for pending to_tier='SCOUT' rows and the unset SCOUT priceId config) could not be run here, but the code itself treats SCOUT as the unpriced free tier, so the defect is real whenever such legacy rows exist.

The diff only shows confirmSubscribe's catch switched to subscriptionErrorI18nKey; handleChangeTier and its catch block are not in the provided hunks, so whether it still shows the generic tierChange error cannot be verified from this code.
